 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Mukthar Ahmed vs Rajesh.N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134499319/
1
Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 24.04.2022 at about 11.30 p.m., the Petitioner being a pedestrian was crossing the road at Jabbar block, near ICICI bank, Vyalikaval Bengaluru, at that time, a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-0296 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result of which, the petitioner had sustained multiple fracture injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
the Petitioner was shifted to Shifaa Hospital, he was treated as an inpatient therein.
He has spent Rs.75,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as auto driver and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The respondent is the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. Despite service of notice, the Respondent remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
6. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.16 and closed his side evidence.

7. Having heard the arguments and upon careful consideration of the entire materials placed on record, following points are taken up for determination of this case:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 24-02-2022 at about 11.30 near ICICI bank, 7th Cross,
Vyalikaval, Bengaluru city, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of rider of Two wheeler bearing No.KA-04-JT- 0296?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so.
How much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?

8. My finding to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
Mukthar Ahmed vs Rajesh.N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134499319/
2 REASONS 9. Point No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 24-04-2022 at about 11.30 p.m. due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-0296.
10.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-16.
He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to 10 are the true copy of FIR, Complaint, statement of victim, spot sketch, Spot mahazar,
notice under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply, IMV report, Wound Certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.11 is the Discharge summary.
Ex.P.12 is the Medical bills.

Ex.P.13 is the advance receipt, Ex.P.14 is 7 medical reports, Ex.P.15 is prescriptions and Ex.P.16 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar card of PW.1.
11.

Upon going through Ex.P.1 & 2 FIR and Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Sadashivanagara Traffic Police Station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the rider of bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-JT-0296 for the offences punishable under Sec.279,
337 of IPC.
The Ex.P3 and 4 are spot sketch and Spot Mahazar show that the concerned police have drawn the mahazar and prepared the sketch in the presence of panchas at the spot.
Upon going through Ex.P.3 sketch exact spot of the accident has been marked.
As per this sketch, the accident was taken place at the middle of the road.
Mahazar discloses that the pedestrian was crossing the road, at that time motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-JT-0296 came with high speed and dashed the pedestrian.
Thereby, the said accident was taken place.
Due to the negligent riding of the rider of the offending two wheeler.
Ex.P.5 is the Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending vehicle and reply notice.
In the reply the Respondent he was riding the offending bike at the time of accident and he also admitted that his bike was not insured.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report, which shows that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects of motor cycle.
The said document further shows that the motor cycle bearing No.KA- 04-JT-0296 was damaged.
These damages justifies the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
The Ex.P.9 is the wound certificate, which shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.

The Ex.P.10 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the Sadashivanagar Traffic Police have Charge-sheeted the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 and 134(A&B), 187, 146, 196 of IPC.
Ex.P.13 is the Discharge summary which shows that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient in Shifaa hospital, Bangalore.

12. The documents Ex.P7 justify the fact that at the time of accident the rider of offending two wheeler had ridden the same without possessing the valid and effective driving licence and policy to the offending vehicle.

The document Ex. P.10 i.e., charge sheet discloses the fact that after thorough investigation IO has charge sheeted the rider of offending two wheeler bearing No.KA-04-JT-0296 as accused No.1 for the offences alleged punishable under Secs.279, 338 of IPC r/w Secs.134(A&B),
187, 146, 196 of IMV Act.
It is evident from the record that till date, the charge sheet Ex. P.10 has remained uncontested and unchallenged.

Moreover, the allegations levelled against the accused person in the charge sheet who is none other than the respondent in this petition justify the fact that the policy of the offending vehicle was not in force at the time of accident and same also disclose that the rider had ridden the said vehicle on the fatal day without possessing valid and effective Driving Mukthar Ahmed vs Rajesh.N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134499319/
3 licence.
13.
Further, it is noted above that inspite of valid service of notice upon them, the respondent has not chosen to contest the petition.
Such being the case, the averments made in the petition and the evidence both oral and documentary placed on hand by the petitioner remained unchallenged and uncontraverted.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-04-JT-0296 by its rider and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
14.
Point No. 2 :

As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 54 years.
He has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.16 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, his year of birth is shown as 1966.
The accident took place on 24.04.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was taken as 56 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
16. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as auto driver and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove his income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
18.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.9 Wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. Multiple abrasion upper and lower limbs with laceration of right forearm

. 
2. Fracture dislocation of the right shoulder with right gracoid process, right acromin process right scapular plate.
Wherein, the Doctor has opined that the said injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
Mukthar Ahmed vs Rajesh.N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134499319/
4 19.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injury sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
20.
The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 24.04.2022 and discharged on 25.04.2022 at Shifaa Hospital, Bengaluru.

21. Upon going through the Discharge summary at Ex.P.11 which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 24.04.2022 and discharged on 25.04.2022 at Shifaa Hospital, Bengaluru. i.e., for 1 day.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 1 days.
22. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, at least it took one month for recovery.
I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500/- under this head (@ Rs.15,500/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
23.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
24. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.75,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 20 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.12 which is totally amounting to Rs.19,034/-.
I have gone through the medical bills.
They found correct.
Hence, the bills are accepted.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.19,100/-. as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

Mukthar Ahmed vs Rajesh.N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134499319/
5 25.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he cannot stand and walk on his own and he is completely disabled, cannot do any work, cannot climb stairs or cannot use his lower part of body, cannot run, and limps while walking, cannot sit on his own and stand independently.
But in order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce evidence.
However, he has not examined any doctor to prove his disability.

The petitioner has claimed sum of Rs.5,00,000/- as compensation by asserting that he has sustained grievous injuries as a result of accident occurred on 24-04-2022 due to the fault of the rider of offending vehicle.
Law expects proof of this aspect regarding the gravity of injuries for which examination of any medical practitioner/doctor is necessary.
However, the petitioner herein has not taken any such pain in getting the treated doctor examined before this court to justify the injuries which according to him has sustained.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any loss of future income under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
26.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs.20,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs.20,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs.15,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.19,100/-
5. Loss of income during the Rs.15,500/-
laid up period 6. Loss of Future income NIL Total Rs.89,600/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.89,600/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

27. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the offending motro cycle bearing No.KA-04-JT-0296.
The respondent being the RC owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".

Mukthar Ahmed vs Rajesh.N on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134499319/
6 28. POINT NO.3 :

sentences.text:
In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.89,600/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
